$meta.title: Figma MCP server + Microsoft Fluent design kits
$meta.description: Grounded reference for connecting the Figma MCP server to a Fluent 2 workflow: which servers exist, what gates access (rate limits + the client catalog allowlist), which tools exist, Microsoft's official Fluent Figma kits, and how a Figma design becomes @fluentui/react-components v9 + Griffel code.
$meta.scope: Read-only reference data. This plugin never registers an OAuth client, never opens a Figma consent screen, and never asks for, stores, proxies, or forwards a Figma token. Auth belongs to the host's own OAuth flow or the signed-in Figma desktop session.

meta.productNameNote: The product is the 'Figma MCP server'. The older name 'Dev Mode MCP server' is retired (the old help URL 302-redirects to the new title). Most published third-party guides are stale and still use the old name and the old tool names (get_code, get_image).
meta.status: Beta. Announced 2025-06-04 in open beta; still labelled beta as of this research (2026-08). Skills/write features carry the note: 'This will eventually be a usage-based paid feature, but is currently available for free during the beta period.'

servers.name: Figma MCP Server (remote / hosted)
servers.quote: We recommend using the Remote MCP server, which connects directly to Figma's hosted endpoint without requiring the Figma desktop app. The remote MCP server also provides the broadest set of features.

requires.figmaPlan: Starter works but is capped at 6 tool calls per month regardless of seat. Professional, Organization, or Enterprise is the realistic floor.
requires.seatType: Dev or Full seat. View and Collab seats get 6 tool calls per month — enough to fail, not enough to work.
requires.note: Remote has no selection-based prompting — every request needs a node-specific link (?node-id=...). A file-only URL fails.

auth.spec: OAuth 2.1 shape: authorization_code + PKCE S256, state required, refresh tokens. Verified from Figma's live public discovery documents.
userSteps: Register the server in your host's MCP config (URL + type only — no secrets).
Start / connect the server in the host, then complete the browser consent (Allow Access).
Re-run the host's auth step if the connection later reports unauthorized.

personalAccessTokens.note: Personal access tokens and the X-Figma-Token header belong to the Figma REST API, not the MCP server. The MCP server's protected-resource metadata declares only Authorization: Bearer with scope mcp:connect. No Figma doc describes putting a PAT in an MCP config.

auth.enterpriseManaged: Enterprise-managed authorization is currently supported only for Claude via Okta Cross App Access (XAA).

prohibitedForThisPlugin: Registering fluent-ui as an OAuth client at https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/mcp/register — only catalog-listed clients may connect, and it would arguably breach the Figma Developer Terms.
Driving or scraping the browser consent screen at https://www.figma.com/oauth/mcp.
Collecting, storing, caching, proxying, or forwarding a Figma PAT or OAuth token.
Injecting Authorization or X-Figma-Token headers into a host config file.
Prompting the user for a Figma token — there is no legitimate MCP use for it.

tools.name: get_design_context
tools.purpose: Primary design-to-code call for a node. Accepts nodeId / fileKey / branchKey (remote: link required), plus clientFrameworks and clientLanguages hints, format and query.
tools.returns: React + Tailwind reference code, a screenshot, and hints. Reference only — not production code.

tools.name: get_variable_defs
tools.purpose: Read the Figma variables and styles used by a selection or node (color, spacing, typography).
tools.returns: Variable/style names and/or values as authored in the file; includes code syntax when the library populates it.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.purpose: Cheap structural probe. Call first for large frames, then re-fetch narrower nodes.
tools.returns: Sparse XML outline of layer IDs, names, types, positions, sizes. With no nodeId it returns the list of top-level pages.

tools.name: get_screenshot
tools.purpose: Visual ground truth for a single node; use it to verify generated code.

tools.name: get_code_connect_map
tools.purpose: Resolve selected instance nodes to real codebase components, when the library owner published Code Connect.
tools.returns: {nodeId: {componentName, source, snippet, snippetImports, snippetNestedFunctions, version, label}}

tools.name: download_assets
tools.purpose: Export images/vectors for up to 20 nodes per call (defaultFormat, defaultScale 0.01–4x).
tools.returns: Temporary URLs for PNG/JPG/SVG/PDF plus raw source images.

tools.name: get_libraries
tools.purpose: Inspect which libraries a file subscribes to and which are available.
tools.returns: Subscribed + available libraries (community UI kits and org libraries).

tools.name: get_motion_context
tools.purpose: Read motion/animation for the same nodeId as get_design_context (recursive option).
tools.returns: Keyframe tracks, easing, CSS @keyframes, motion.dev snippets.

tools.name: whoami
tools.purpose: Diagnose entitlement before a big job. Rate-limit exempt.
tools.returns: Email, all plans, and seat type per plan.

tools.name: get_context_for_code_connect
tools.returns: Property definitions with types and variant options, plus the descendant tree.

tools.name: use_figma
tools.purpose: General-purpose write-to-canvas via the Plugin API.
tools.returns: Write result (20 KB output response limit per call).

tools.name: generate_figma_design
tools.purpose: Write — generate a design. Select clients only. Rate-limit exempt.

prompts.name: create_design_system_rules
prompts.note: This is an MCP prompt, not a tool — an agent cannot call it like a tool, and 'Not all agents and clients support MCP prompts.' Its output must be saved to the host's rules/ or instructions/ path. Do not depend on it; the fluent-figma skill ships the equivalent Fluent ruleset up front.
prompts.hostInvocation: VS Code invokes MCP prompts as /<server>.<prompt>.

limits: Rate limited per seat and plan — see rateLimits. whoami, add_code_connect_map, and generate_figma_design are exempt.
Remote is link-based only: no selection-based prompting. A node-specific link (?node-id=...) is required.
Asset URLs returned by get_design_context expire in about 7 days.
download_assets caps at 20 nodes per call; scale range 0.01–4x.
Large selections truncate — call get_metadata first, then re-fetch narrower nodes.
use_figma has a 20 KB output response limit per call, no image support in write yet, and fonts must be uploaded to the Figma account.
Write-to-canvas is limited to Full and Dev seats on paid plans; Dev seats are read-only outside drafts.
The server is explicitly not designed to return production-ready code.

servers.name: Figma MCP Server (local / desktop)
servers.quote: Figma provides the local desktop version of the Figma MCP server for some specific organization and enterprise use cases, but we strongly recommend using the remote version.
servers.positioning: Niche. Choose it only for the specific org/enterprise cases Figma calls out, or when you need selection-based prompting.

requires.figmaPlan: Same rate limits as remote — Starter is 6 calls/month regardless of seat.
requires.seatType: Dev or Full seat strongly recommended; View/Collab = 6 calls/month.
requires.note: Enable it in the Figma desktop app: open a Design file, toggle Dev Mode (Shift+D), then inspect panel > MCP server > Enable desktop MCP server. The server only exists while the desktop app runs.

userSteps: Sign in to the Figma desktop app.
Open a Design file and toggle Dev Mode (Shift+D).
Enable the desktop MCP server from the inspect panel.
auth.note: No auth parameter appears anywhere in the local install docs — the config is a bare loopback URL with no headers. It is implicitly authenticated by the signed-in desktop session. (Figma never states this explicitly; it is inference from the absence of any documented credential mechanism.)

toolsNotAvailable: all write-to-canvas and Code Connect authoring tools
advantages: Selection-based prompting works (the remote server is link-only).
limits: Requires the Figma desktop app to be installed, running, and in Dev Mode.
Fewer tools than remote — no asset download, no design-system search, no whoami.
The legacy /sse endpoint from the June 2025 beta is not in current docs. Use /mcp.
Same seat/plan rate limits as remote.

rateLimits.note: 6 tool calls per month. Enough to fail, not enough to work.
6 tool calls per month — the seat type caps you, not the plan.
Starter has no Dev/Full tier in Figma's table; a Starter user is capped at 6 calls/month regardless of seat.
The realistic floor for actual work.
Also the minimum plan for Code Connect.

entitlementSummary: Access is a rate limit, not an on/off switch. Anyone can connect; a Starter/View/Collab user simply runs out after ~6 calls in a month — often mid-task. Tell users this before they start. Diagnose with whoami (rate-limit exempt, reports email, plans, and seat type per plan).

catalogGate.what: Figma MCP Catalog — an allowlist of MCP clients permitted to connect to the Figma MCP server.
catalogGate.whoCanConnect: Only clients listed in the Figma MCP Catalog. A developer wanting to add a new client must join Figma's waitlist.
catalogGate.quote: Only clients listed in the Figma MCP Catalog can connect to the Figma MCP Server. If you're a developer interested in connecting a new MCP client, you can join the waitlist.
catalogGate.implication: This is a hard gate on which of our hosts can use Figma MCP at all, and it is not something this plugin can work around. fluent-ui cannot register itself as an OAuth client via the DCR endpoint, and writing a correct config entry into a non-catalog host will still fail at authorization. Confirmation comes from Figma publishing first-party install instructions for a host; hosts Figma never documents are unconfirmed, not supported-by-default.
catalogGate.appliesTo: both the remote and the local/desktop server
catalogGate.catalogListNote: The catalog page is JS-rendered and the client table in help article 32132100833559 did not render, so the full client list could not be read directly. Host confirmation below is therefore based on Figma publishing first-party install instructions for that host.

hosts.name: VS Code
hosts.configPath: user mcp.json (MCP: Open User Configuration) or .vscode/mcp.json
hosts.authStep: Start the figma server in the MCP view, then Allow Access in the browser.
hosts.note: VS Code requires GitHub Copilot enabled on your account to use MCP. Figma's VS Code doc also shows an optional "inputs": [] sibling key.

hosts.name: VS Code Insiders
hosts.note: Same dialect as VS Code, but Figma names only 'VS Code'. Whether Insiders is a distinct catalog client is unconfirmed.

hosts.name: VSCodium
hosts.note: Same dialect as VS Code; catalog listing unconfirmed. VSCodium also lacks the GitHub Copilot prerequisite path.

hosts.name: Cursor
hosts.authStep: Settings > MCP > Connect > Open > Allow access.
hosts.note: Cursor infers HTTP from url; Figma's official snippet omits type. Figma's preferred path is the Cursor plugin: type /add-plugin figma in agent chat (bundles MCP config + skills + asset rules).

hosts.name: Claude Code
hosts.cli: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp
hosts.note: type is MANDATORY here: an entry with a url and no type is read as stdio and hard-fails ('MCP server "<name>" has a "url" but no "type"; add "type": "http"'). streamable-http is accepted as an alias for http. Figma also ships a plugin: claude plugin install figma@claude-plugins-official.

hosts.name: Codex
hosts.authStep: Authenticate when prompted after adding the server.
hosts.note: Figma documents the CLI command only; no on-disk config shape was verified.

hosts.name: Gemini CLI
hosts.note: Gemini's dialect uses httpUrl (NOT url) plus an explicit oauth block — verified from figma/mcp-server-guide:gemini-extension.json.

hosts.name: Claude Desktop
hosts.authStep: Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector (handles OAuth).
hosts.note: Different from Claude Code. claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers is stdio-only, so a raw url entry there will NOT work — do not write one. Figma documents Claude Code only. A community npx mcp-remote stdio bridge exists but is unverified for Figma.

hosts.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
hosts.authStep: Unconfirmed — whether Copilot CLI performs the Figma OAuth dance was not verified.
hosts.note: The http entry shape is verified from github/github-mcp-server's own remote-server example (Copilot CLI's type vocabulary is local/http, not VS Code's stdio). But Figma does not list Copilot CLI in any install doc, so catalog eligibility is unconfirmed.

hosts.name: Windsurf
hosts.authStep: Unconfirmed — Windsurf's native OAuth handling for remote MCP was not verified.
hosts.note: Windsurf uses serverUrl, NOT url — the wrong key fails silently. Secondary sources only; not in Figma's docs.

hosts.name: Cline
hosts.configPath: cline_mcp_settings.json (path varies by VS Code profile — detect, don't guess)
hosts.note: Cline uses streamableHttp (camelCase) — different from Claude Code's streamable-http. Secondary sources only; not in Figma's docs.

hosts.name: Google Antigravity
hosts.note: Not mentioned anywhere in the research. No config shape and no catalog status — do not guess.

hosts.name: Visual Studio 2022/2026
hosts.note: Not mentioned anywhere in the research. No config shape and no catalog status — do not guess.

hosts.name: Xcode 27 beta
hosts.authStep: Install the plug-in from https://github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide, then authorize.
hosts.note: Documented by Figma but not a host this plugin targets. Listed for completeness.

hostConfigNotes: Never write 'sse' for Figma — Claude Code marks SSE deprecated and Figma publishes only /mcp endpoints.
Figma's generic fallback for undocumented editors is { "mcpServers": { "figma": { "url": "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp" } } }. It is a shape, not a claim of catalog support.

The fluent-ui Claude-style template documents type as omitted (hosts/README.md). That is correct for stdio but breaks for an HTTP url entry in Claude Code — always emit "type": "http" for HTTP entries.
A Figma entry should always be opt-in (e.g. a --with-figma flag). Silently adding a third-party network endpoint to a user's config is surprising.
Never write an Authorization or X-Figma-Token header into a host config file — these files are plaintext and often synced.

codeConnect.purpose: Maps a Figma component to the real component in your codebase, so get_design_context returns your component instead of generic markup.
codeConnect.fluentSupportDetail: No official Microsoft-published Code Connect mappings for Fluent were found. Code searches for figma.connect, @figma/code-connect in org:microsoft, and Fluent-specific .figma.tsx files all returned zero results. No community Fluent Code Connect project was found either. Absence of evidence in code search is not absolute proof — a mapping could exist inside Microsoft's own Figma library without a public repo — but do not claim Microsoft ships Code Connect for Fluent.
codeConnect.publishingConstraint: Code Connect must be published to a Figma library by the file owner, so Microsoft would have to publish it into the community kits — and Code Connect requires Org/Enterprise.
codeConnect.howItHelps: Without Code Connect, get_design_context cannot know that a Figma 'Button' is @fluentui/react-components' <Button appearance="primary">. It emits generic React + Tailwind instead. The fluent-figma skill closes that gap by name mapping; Code Connect closes it deterministically.
codeConnect.diyPath: A team on Org/Enterprise can duplicate the Fluent kit into their own library and author Code Connect against @fluentui/react-components themselves. That is the only route to deterministic component identity today.
codeConnect.fileFormatNote: Figma's current Code Connect skill emits .figma.ts parserless templates using figma.code`...`, NOT .figma.tsx + figma.connect(). Its own skill states output written as .figma.tsx is rejected outright.

fluentFigmaResources.name: Fluent 1 / Fluent UI React v8 Figma kit
fluentFigmaResources.note: COULD NOT VERIFY. Microsoft's current resources page lists only Fluent 2 kits; web search returned four mutually inconsistent community file IDs (a hallucination signature), and https://aka.ms/FluentToolkits/Web/Figma redirects to a dead 2020 Sketch zip. fluentKitTiers.role: The source of truth for Fluent and Copilot design styling decisions inclusive of color, stroke width, corner radius, spacing, and size tokens. Houses the global and alias Figma variables and drives light/dark toggling.
Code-aligned building blocks for web, iOS, and Android.

fluentKitTiersImplication: Tokens live in a SEPARATE library file from the component kits. The designer's file must have BOTH the Fluent 2 Core UI Kit and the Fluent 2 design language library enabled, or get_variable_defs returns unresolved or partial names.

designToFluentCode: Preflight: confirm the Figma MCP tools (get_design_context et al.) are actually present in this host. If they are not, tell the user to register and authenticate the Figma MCP server — never fabricate design data.
Check entitlement early: call whoami (rate-limit exempt) to read seat type and plan. On a View/Collab seat or Starter plan, warn the user they have ~6 calls for the whole month before spending any.
Require a node-specific link. The designer right-clicks the frame > Copy link to selection, producing a ?node-id=... URL. Reject file-only URLs — remote has no selection-based prompting.
Confirm the file has BOTH the Fluent 2 Core UI Kit and the Fluent 2 design language library enabled, or variables will not resolve.
For a large frame, call get_metadata first and pick narrower node IDs — large selections truncate.
Call get_code_connect_map first. If the user has their own Code Connect, its snippet wins over everything else.
Call get_design_context with clientFrameworks: "React" and clientLanguages set, so the right mappings and hints come back.
Call get_variable_defs to get the design tokens actually used.
Call get_screenshot for visual ground truth.
Call download_assets (remote only) for images/vectors — do not hand-draw SVG. Asset URLs expire in about 7 days, so save them into the repo immediately.
TRANSLATE, never paste. Emit @fluentui/react-components v9 + Griffel makeStyles + tokens.*. Never emit Tailwind classes into a Fluent project.
Wrap the surface in FluentProvider with webLightTheme/webDarkTheme; take icons from @fluentui/react-icons; convert Auto Layout to flex with spacing tokens.
Verify: diff the rendered result against get_screenshot, then run the fluent_accessibility_checklist.
figmaOutputPriorityOrder: Code Connect snippets — use the mapped codebase component directly.
Design annotations — follow the designer's notes.
Design tokens (CSS variables) — map them to the project's token system.
Raw hex / absolute positioning — lean on the screenshot.
workflow.tokenMapping: get_variable_defs returns the Figma variable name and value as authored in the file — Fluent 2 kits use a global/alias model, so expect path-style names (for example Brand/Background/Default or Spacing/Horizontal/M) rather than colorBrandBackground or spacingHorizontalM. The real bridge is Figma's 'code syntax' feature: each variable can carry one name per platform (Web, Android, iOS), and Figma states that if code syntax is provided, the MCP server can give that exact code to the LLM. So: (1) prefer any code syntax value returned by get_variable_defs; (2) otherwise map the variable path to the Fluent token by name — Brand/Background/Default -> tokens.colorBrandBackground, Spacing/Horizontal/M -> tokens.spacingHorizontalM, corner radius -> tokens.borderRadius*, elevation -> tokens.shadow*; (3) confirm the exact token with the fluent_get_token / fluent_list_tokens MCP tools; (4) never emit a raw hex or px value that duplicates a token. Whether Microsoft actually populates code syntax in the published kits is UNVERIFIED — plan for name mapping.

qualityTiers.result: Generic React + Tailwind with hardcoded hex values.
Real @fluentui/react-components + tokens.* via name mapping, with occasional misses. This is where most users live — optimize for it.

qualityTiers.setup: Silver + the user's own Code Connect on a duplicated Fluent library
qualityTiers.result: Near-deterministic component selection. Requires Org/Enterprise plus publishing rights.

gotchas.cause: No Code Connect, so the agent has no component identity.
gotchas.fix: Apply the fluent-figma component-identity mapping: match the Figma component name + variant props to the Fluent v9 component + props.

gotchas.cause: Figma variable names differ from Fluent token names, and code syntax may be absent.
gotchas.fix: Map by name and confirm with fluent_get_token. Never ship the hex.

gotchas.symptom: Inline styles or Tailwind classes instead of Griffel makeStyles
gotchas.cause: The agent defaults to the Tailwind idiom of the reference output.
gotchas.fix: Rewrite into makeStyles; Tailwind must never land in a Fluent project.

gotchas.cause: Not expressible in a Figma frame.
gotchas.fix: Add FluentProvider with webLightTheme/webDarkTheme at the app root.

gotchas.cause: The source frame lacked Auto Layout.
gotchas.fix: Rebuild as flex/grid with spacing tokens; ask the designer to add Auto Layout.
Import from @fluentui/react-icons; use download_assets only for genuine imagery.

gotchas.symptom: Variables come back unresolved or partially named
gotchas.cause: The file does not have the Fluent 2 design language library enabled alongside the Core UI Kit.
gotchas.fix: Ask the designer to enable both libraries.

gotchas.cause: Asset URLs from get_design_context expire in about 7 days.

gotchas.symptom: Truncated or empty design context on a big frame
gotchas.fix: get_metadata first, then re-fetch narrower node IDs.

gotchas.cause: View/Collab seat or Starter plan — 6 calls per month.
gotchas.fix: There is no fix in-tool. Warn up front and check whoami first.

gotchas.symptom: Server connects but every call is unauthorized
gotchas.cause: The host is not in the Figma MCP Catalog, or OAuth was never completed.
gotchas.fix: Complete the host's own auth step; if the host is not catalog-listed, it cannot connect at all.

gotchas.symptom: iOS/Android/Windows kit output rendered as React
gotchas.fix: Fluent 2 iOS kit -> fluentui-apple (SwiftUI/UIKit); Fluent Android kit -> fluentui-android Compose; Windows UI Kit -> WinUI 3. Figma also ships a figma-swiftui skill for iOS.

workflow.designedNotToShipCode: Figma is explicit that this is by design: 'The MCP server is designed to provide Figma context and is language and framework agnostic... the server isn't designed to return production-ready code... This format resembles react-like code because AI agents are commonly trained on large amounts of web-based data.' Figma's own skill repeats it: 'The returned code is React + Tailwind enriched with hints. You MUST treat it as a REFERENCE, not as final code to paste verbatim.'
